title: Prediction of peak power output on the cycle ergometer using demographic, anthropometric and biological parameters for the individualization of ramp protocols in spiroergometric performance diagnostics
summary: Spiroergometry is a clinical procedure that is regularly used in routine sports medicine examinations due to its high diagnostic, prognostic and functional significance. During physical exertion, the respiratory gases are measured and the heart, circulation, respiration, metabolism and cardiopulmonary performance are examined. In addition to diagnostic findings for patients, this method is also a preventive procedure to provide advice and guidance for amateur athletes, competitive athletes and for rehabilitation sports (cf. Kroidl et al., 2015). The primary aim of the present research project is to create objectively collected guidelines for the individualized implementation of spiroergometric endurance performance diagnostics. As no guidelines for the individualized design of spiroergometric endurance protocols exist in sports science practice to date (American College of Sports Medicne, 2017; Balady et al., 2010), the present project will use different methods to calculate and compare predictive models for peak power output (Pmax) achievable in an endurance test on a cycle ergometer.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
no entry
Exclusion criteria:
Since the prediction models for Pmax should also be applicable to as many different populations as possible in the follow-up, the exclusion criteria are limited to physical and mental conditions that make it impossible for subjects to participate in the planned studies. These include:
- Acute infections or orthopedic problems that make spiroergometric exercise impossible,
- the wearing of a pacemaker or an ongoing pregnancy, as this makes it impossible to perform a bioimpedance analysis to determine the body composition,
- lack of knowledge of German, as it makes it impossible to answer the questionnaires.
Non-orthopedic medical conditions, such as metabolic, neurologic, or neoplastic diseases, are not grounds for exclusion.
